label: 0052 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over 53 windows): 0051 with the public seafloor GNSS-A positions as data and Japan Trench afterslip after Tohoku allowed in either sense, uncorrelated noise, background coupling from −1 to 1, fourteen slow slip events as signal, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0051 with the Japan Coast Guard's 27 SGO-A sites (2000–2024) and Tohoku University's G02–G20 (2012–2024) fitted as data. Without them, 0051 fails beneath the Japan Trench forearc after Tohoku: from 2013 to 2021 the sites near the trench move landward faster than the plate converges. Here the Tohoku afterslip state on the Japan Trench takes either sign, so coupling can exceed 1 off Miyagi after Tohoku (1.44 on average in 2012–2021): a kinematic stand-in for the landward pull of relaxation near the trench, not locking. Seafloor residuals beneath the Japan Trench after Tohoku fall from 112 and 162 mm to 28 and 49 mm, Nankai from 31 to 28 mm, and the onshore fit matches 0051's. Held-out seafloor sites are predicted far better than by 0051; onshore window cross-validation is 415 lower. A BEL sheet at the base of the subducting plate fits the seafloor as well but costs more onshore, so it isn't used. Seafloor data: Japan Coast Guard (CC BY-NC 4.0) and Tohoku University (CC BY 4.0).
